layer.name: VK_LAYER_LUNARG_api_dump
layer.introduction: The API Dump utility layer prints API calls, parameters, and values to the identified output stream.

presets.label: Text Output
presets.description: Output API dump to a text file

presets.label: HTML Output
presets.description: Output API dump to a HTML file

presets.label: JSON Output
presets.description: Output API dump to a JSON file

settings.label: Output Range
settings.description: Comma separated list of frames to output or a range of frames with a start, count, and optional interval separated by a dash. A count of 0 will output every frame after the start of the range. Example: "5-8-2" will output frame 5, continue until frame 13, dumping every other frame. Example: "3,8-2" will output frames 3, 8, and 9.

settings.label: Output Format
settings.description: Specifies the format used for output; can be HTML, JSON, or  Text (default -- outputs plain text)

flags.label: Text
flags.description: Plain text

flags.label: HTML
flags.description: HTML

flags.label: JSON
flags.description: Json

settings.label: Pre-dump the parameters.
settings.description: Setting this to true causes parameters to calls be logged before the function as well as after the function.

settings.label: Output to File
settings.description: Setting this to true indicates that output should be written to file instead of stdout

settings.label: Log Filename
settings.description: Specifies the file to dump to when output files are enabled

settings.label: Log Flush After Write
settings.description: Setting this to true causes IO to be flushed after each API call that is written

settings.label: Name Size
settings.description: The number of characters the name of a variable should consume, assuming more are not required

settings.label: Show Types
settings.description: Dump types in addition to values

settings.label: Type Size
settings.description: The number of characters the name of a type should consume, assuming more are not required

settings.label: Show Timestamp
settings.description: Show the timestamp of function calls since start in microseconds

settings.label: Show Shader
settings.description: Dump the shader binary code in pCode as an hex array which can be viewed in https://www.khronos.org/spir/visualizer/

settings.label: Show Parameter Details
settings.description: Dump parameter details in addition to API calls

settings.label: Hide Addresses
settings.description: Dump "address" in place of hex addresses

settings.label: Use Spaces
settings.description: Setting this to true causes all tab characters to be replaced with spaces

settings.label: Indent Size
settings.description: Specifies the number of spaces that a tab is equal to

settings.label: Show Thread and Frame
settings.description: Show the thread and frame of each function called

layer.name: VK_LAYER_LUNARG_gfxreconstruct
layer.introduction: The GFXReconstruct Capture Layer intercepts Vulkan API calls and logs them to a capture file. Other tools in the GFXReconstruct suite can inspect, modify, or replay capture files generated by this component.

presets.label: Range
presets.description: Capture a range of frames between presses of the F5 key.

settings.label: Hotkey Capture Trigger
settings.description: Specify a hotkey (any one of F1-F12, TAB, CONTROL) that will be used to start/stop capture. Example: F3 will set the capture trigger to F3 hotkey. One capture file will be generated for each pair of start/stop hotkey presses. Default is: Empty string (hotkey capture trigger is disabled).

flags.label: F1
flags.description: F1 Key

flags.label: F2
flags.description: F2 Key

flags.label: F3
flags.description: F3 Key

flags.label: F4
flags.description: F4 Key

flags.label: F5
flags.description: F5 Key

flags.label: F6
flags.description: F6 Key

flags.label: F7
flags.description: F7 Key

flags.label: F8
flags.description: F8 Key

flags.label: F9
flags.description: F9 Key

flags.label: F10
flags.description: F10 Key

flags.label: F11
flags.description: F11 Key

flags.label: F12
flags.description: F12 Key

flags.label: TAB
flags.description: TAB Key

flags.label: CONTROL
flags.description: CONTROL Key

settings.label: Capture Trigger Boundary
settings.description: Select the boundary where GFXReconstruct checks for capture-trigger state changes.

flags.label: Frames
flags.description: Check capture triggers at frame boundaries.

flags.label: Queue Submits
flags.description: Check capture triggers at queue-submit boundaries.

settings.label: Capture Trigger Boundary Limit
settings.description: Specify a limit on the number of capture boundaries to record after the trigger starts capture. Boundaries are frames by default and queue submits when capture_trigger_boundary is queue_submits. Default is: Empty string (no limit)

settings.label: Capture Specific Frames
settings.description: Specify one or more comma-separated frame ranges to capture. Each range will be written to its own file. A frame range can be specified as a single value, to specify a single frame to capture, or as two hyphenated values, to specify the first and last frame to capture. Frame ranges should be specified in ascending order and cannot overlap. Note that frame numbering is 1-based (i.e. the first frame is frame 1). Example: 200,301-305 will create two capture files, one containing a single frame and one containing five frames. Default is: Empty string (all frames are captured).

settings.label: Capture Specific process
settings.description: Specify one process name to capture.

settings.label: Capture File Name
settings.description: Path to use when creating the capture file. Default is: gfxrecon_capture.gfxr

settings.label: Capture File Name with Timestamp
settings.description: Add a timestamp (yyyymmddThhmmss) postfix to the capture file name.

settings.label: Capture File Flush After Write
settings.description: Flush output stream after each packet is written to the capture file. Default is: false.

settings.label: Compression Format
settings.description: Compression format to use with the capture file. Valid values are: LZ4, ZLIB, ZSTD, and NONE. Default is: LZ4

flags.label: LZ4
flags.description: Fastest compression algorithm that favors performance over compression ratio.

flags.label: ZLIB
flags.description: Widely used compression algorithm with better compression ratio than LZ4 but worse performance.

flags.label: ZSTD
flags.description: Newer compression algorithm with better compression ratio and performance than ZLIB, though not as fast as LZ4.

flags.label: NONE
flags.description: No compression

settings.label: Capture Environment
settings.description: List of environment variables to capture.

settings.label: Memory Tracking Mode
settings.description: Specifies the memory tracking mode to use for detecting modifications to mapped Vulkan memory objects. Available options are: page_guard, assisted, and unassisted.

flags.label: page_guard
flags.description: Tracks modifications to individual memory pages, which are written to the capture file on calls to vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges, vkUnmapMemory, and vkQueueSubmit. Tracking modifications requires allocating shadow memory for all mapped memory.

flags.label: assisted
flags.description: Expects the application to call vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges after memory is modified; the memory ranges specified to the vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges call will be written to the capture file during the call.

flags.label: unassisted
flags.description: Writes the full content of mapped memory to the capture file on calls to vkUnmapMemory and vkQueueSubmit. It is very inefficient and may be unusable with real-world applications that map large amounts of memory.

settings.label: Page Guard Copy on Map
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, copies the content of the mapped memory to the shadow memory immediately after the memory is mapped.

settings.label: Page Guard Separate Read Tracking
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, copies the content of pages accessed for read from mapped memory to shadow memory on each read. Can overwrite unprocessed shadow memory content when an application is reading from and writing to the same page.

settings.label: Page Guard External Memory
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, use the VK_EXT_external_memory_host extension to eliminate the need for shadow memory allocations. For each memory allocation from a host visible memory type, the capture layer will create an allocation from system memory, which it can monitor for write access, and provide that allocation to vkAllocateMemory as external memory. Only available on Windows.

settings.label: Page Guard Persistent Memory
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, this option changes the way that the shadow memory used to detect modifications to mapped memory is allocated. The default behavior is to allocate and copy the mapped memory range on map and free the allocation on unmap. When this option is enabled, an allocation with a size equal to that of the object being mapped is made once on the first map and is not freed until the object is destroyed. This option is intended to be used with applications that frequently map and unmap large memory ranges, to avoid frequent allocation and copy operations that can have a negative impact on performance. This option is ignored when GFXRECON_PAGE_GUARD_EXTERNAL_MEMORY is enabled.

settings.label: Page Guard Align Buffer Sizes
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, this option overrides the Vulkan API calls that report buffer memory properties to report that buffer sizes and alignments must be a multiple of the system page size. This option is intended to be used with applications that perform CPU writes and GPU writes/copies to different buffers that are bound to the same page of mapped memory, which may result in data being lost when copying pages from the page_guard shadow allocation to the real allocation. This data loss can result in visible corruption during capture. Forcing buffer sizes and alignments to a multiple of the system page size prevents multiple buffers from being bound to the same page, avoiding data loss from simultaneous CPU writes to the shadow allocation and GPU writes to the real allocation for different buffers bound to the same page. This option is only available for the Vulkan API.

settings.label: Page Guard unblock SIGSEGV from thread's signal mask
settings.description: When the page_guard memory tracking mode is enabled, this option overrides enables SIGSEGV in thread's signal mask in the case that it has been disabled.

settings.label: Log

settings.label: Level
settings.description: Specify the minimum severity level of messages to log. Options are: debug, info, warning, error, and fatal. The specified level and all higher levels will be enabled for logging. For example, choosing the warning level will also enable the error and fatal levels.

settings.label: Log File

layer.name: VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation
layer.introduction:
The main, comprehensive Khronos validation layer.

Vulkan is an Explicit API, enabling direct control over how GPUs actually work. By design, minimal error checking is done inside a Vulkan driver. Applications have full control and responsibility for correct operation. Any errors in how Vulkan is used can result in a crash. 

The Khronos Validation Layer can be enabled to assist development by enabling developers to verify their applications correctly use the Vulkan API.

presets.label: Core Validation
presets.description: The same as Default settings but some fields are not reset when switching between presets (Debug Action, Duplicated Message).

presets.label: Synchronization Only
presets.description: Identify resource access conflicts due to missing or incorrect synchronization operations between actions reading or writing the same regions of memory.

presets.label: GPU-Assisted Validation (GPU-AV)
presets.description: Check for API usage errors at shader execution time.

presets.label: Debug Printf Only
presets.description: Debug shader code by "printing" any values of interest to the debug callback or stdout.

presets.label: GPU Dump Only
presets.description: Turn on only GPU Dump and turn off everything else.

presets.label: Legacy Detection Only
presets.description: Turn off everything but legacy detection.

presets.label: Best Practices Only
presets.description: Provides warnings on valid API usage that is potential API misuse.

settings.label: CPU Centric Validation
settings.description: Control the Validation done only on the CPU

settings.label: Core
settings.description: The main, heavy-duty validation checks. This may be valuable early in the development cycle to reduce validation output while correcting parameter/object usage errors.

settings.label: Image Layout
settings.description: Check that the layout of each image subresource is correct whenever it is used by a command buffer. These checks are very CPU intensive for some applications.

settings.label: Command Buffer State
settings.description: Check that all Vulkan objects used by a command buffer have not been destroyed. These checks can be CPU intensive for some applications.

settings.label: Object in Use
settings.description: Check that Vulkan objects are not in use by a command buffer when they are destroyed.

settings.label: Query
settings.description: Checks for commands that use VkQueryPool objects.

settings.label: Shader
settings.description: This will validate the contents of the SPIR-V which can be CPU intensive during application start up. This does internal checks as well as calling spirv-val. (Same effect using VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADERS_EXT)

settings.label: Caching
settings.description: Creates an internal instance of VK_EXT_validation_cache and upon vkDestroyInstance, will cache the shader validation so sequential usage of the validation layers will be skipped.

settings.label: Disable spirv-val
settings.description: Allows normal shader validation to run, but removes just spirv-val for performance reasons

messages.title: Validation layer performance issue
messages.description: Both 'Core validation' and 'GPU-assisted validation' are enabled. This is going to require a lot of CPU resource causing the Vulkan application to run very slowly.
messages.informative: Are you sure you want to enable 'Core Validation'?

settings.label: Synchronization
settings.description: Check for resource access conflicts caused by missing or incorrectly used synchronization operations.

settings.label: Full validation
settings.description: Validate all accesses. Errors are reported during queue submission.

settings.label: Record-time reporting
settings.description: Report errors during command buffer recording, at the command that caused them. This runs a subset of full validation and adds CPU overhead. Disabling it does not reduce validation coverage. Full validation reports errors during queue submission.

settings.label: Submit-time validation (deprecated)
settings.description: Deprecated, use Full validation instead. When present it sets Full validation.

settings.label: Shader accesses heuristic
settings.description: Take into account memory accesses performed by the shader based on SPIR-V static analysis. Warning: can produce false-positives, can ignore certain types of accesses, does not support VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer.

settings.label: LoadOp after StoreOp validation
settings.description: Detect LoadOp after StoreOp hazards between render pass instances.

settings.label: Error messages
settings.description: Options to configure synchronization validation error reporting

settings.label: Extra properties
settings.description: Append a section of key-value properties to the error message. Useful for filtering errors.

settings.label: Stateless Parameter
settings.description: Stateless parameter checks. This may not always be necessary late in a development cycle.

settings.label: Object Lifetime
settings.description: Object tracking checks. This may not always be necessary late in a development cycle.

settings.label: Thread Safety
settings.description: Thread checks. In order to not degrade performance, it might be best to run your program with thread-checking disabled most of the time, enabling it occasionally for a quick sanity check or when debugging difficult application behaviors.

settings.label: Handle Wrapping
settings.description: Handle wrapping checks. Disable this feature if you are experiencing crashes when creating new extensions or developing new Vulkan objects/structures.

settings.label: Legacy Detection
settings.description: Give warnings when using legacy parts of the API.

settings.label: When to give warning
settings.description: Control when legacy detection warnings are emitted

flags.label: Always
flags.description: Give warning any time using the superseded functionality.

flags.label: Only supported
flags.description: Only give warning if the instance/device supports the superseded functionality.

flags.label: Only enabled
flags.description: Only give warning if you enabled the superseded functionality extensions/version.

messages.title: Warning: Legacy Detection without warning level message severity
messages.description: Enabling Legacy Detection, but the 'warning' level message severity is disabled, so messages won't be shown.
messages.informative: Do you want to add 'warning' level to 'Message Severity'?

settings.label: Best Practices
settings.description: Outputs warnings related to common misuse of the API, but which are not explicitly prohibited by the specification.

settings.label: ARM-specific best practices
settings.description: Outputs warnings for spec-conforming but non-ideal code on ARM GPUs.

settings.label: AMD-specific best practices
settings.description: Outputs warnings for spec-conforming but non-ideal code on AMD GPUs.

settings.label: IMG-specific best practices
settings.description: Outputs warnings for spec-conforming but non-ideal code on Imagination GPUs.

settings.label: NVIDIA-specific best practices
settings.description: Outputs warnings for spec-conforming but non-ideal code on NVIDIA GPUs.

settings.label: GPU Centric Validation
settings.description: Control the Validation for GPU centric API

settings.label: GPU Assisted Validation (GPU-AV)
settings.description: Enable validation that cannot be done the CPU and needs hooks into the GPU execution

settings.label: Safe Mode
settings.description: Will have GPU-AV try and prevent crashes, but will be much slower to validate. If using Safe Mode, consider using selective shader instrumentation, to only instrument the shaders/pipelines causing issues.

settings.label: Force on robustness features
settings.description: This will enable all possible robustness features for the app at device creation time. This can be used to quickly detect if with robustness, your issue disappears. GPU-AV will also skip validating things already covered by robustness, so turning on should reduce GPU-AV performance overhead.

settings.label: Shader instrumentation
settings.description: Instrument shaders to validate descriptors, descriptor indexing, buffer device addresses and ray queries. Warning: will considerably slow down shader executions.

settings.label: Descriptors indexing
settings.description: Enable descriptors and buffer out of bounds validation when using descriptor indexing

settings.label: Post process descriptor indexing
settings.description: Track which descriptor indexes were used in shader to run normal validation afterwards

settings.label: Out of bounds buffer device addresses
settings.description: Check for invalid access using buffer device address

settings.label: Mesh Shading SPIR-V instructions
settings.description: Enable shader instrumentation on VK_EXT_mesh_shader

settings.label: TraceRay SPIR-V instructions
settings.description: Enable shader instrumentation on OpTraceRayKHR, OpHitObject*, OpReportIntersectionKHR, OpRayQueryInitializeKHR

settings.label: Out of bounds vertex attribute fetching
settings.description: Validate that no vertex attribute fetching is out of bonds

settings.label: Shader Sanitizer
settings.description: Things invalid to do in SPIR-V but don't have a dedicated check (example: dividing an int by zero, reaching OpUnreachable, invalid casting, overflow/undeflow). When in safe mode, will modify the invalid usage.

settings.label: Shared Memory Data Race Detection
settings.description: Detects data races on shared memory (Compute shaders only). Limitations: This does not handle mixing atomics and non-atomics on the same locations without a barrier in between, this could lead to false positives. This assumes barrier() is used for all shared memory synchronization.

settings.label: Maximum Indices
settings.description: Number of indices held in the buffer used to index commands and validation resources (Max number of draws/dispatches in a command buffer that can be tracked). Can be lowered to save memory.

settings.label: Lower Device Limits for Unit Testing
settings.description: Only for use by the Validation Layer test suite, ignore otherwise.

settings.label: Buffer content validation
settings.description: Validate buffers containing parameters used in indirect Vulkan commands, or used in copy commands

settings.label: Indirect draws parameters
settings.description: Validate buffers containing draw parameters used in indirect draw commands. Includes vkCmdDrawMeshTasks* calls as well

settings.label: Indirect dispatches parameters
settings.description: Validate buffers containing dispatch parameters used in indirect dispatch commands

settings.label: Indirect trace rays parameters
settings.description: Validate buffers containing ray tracing parameters used in indirect ray tracing commands

settings.label: Buffer copies
settings.description: Validate copies involving a VkBuffer. Right now only validates copy buffer to image.

settings.label: VK_KHR_copy_memory_indirect
settings.description: Validate VK_KHR_copy_memory_indirect.

settings.label: Index buffers
settings.description: Validate that indexed draws do not fetch indices outside of the bounds of the index buffer.

settings.label: Acceleration structures builds
settings.description: Validate acceleration structures references in TLAS build commands.

settings.label: Ray tracing buffers consistency
settings.description: Validate that between a BLAS build and its update, triangle geometries using index buffer keep its content identical (VUID 03768), and that active/inactive primitives do not change this status (VUIDs 03663 and 03664). Warning: a record of vertex/index buffers will be maintained in device local memory, so validation can be GPU memory heavy.

settings.label: Scoped GPU-AV
settings.description: Reduce the scope of GPU-AV allowing it to be must faster.

settings.label: Selective Instrument Shaders
settings.description:
When turned on, shaders are NOT instrumented unless selected. This can be done by:
- passing a VkValidationFeaturesEXT struct in the pNext of VkShaderModuleCreateInfo/VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo/vkCreateShadersEXT pNext
- using a regex matching a shader/pipeline debug name.
- Providing a CDL dump file to parse the debug names from it.

settings.label: Developer Debug Settings
settings.description: GPU-AV debug settings

settings.label: Disable all of GPU-AV
settings.description: Acts as a VkValidationFeatureDisableEXT to override the VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_GPU_ASSISTED_EXT passed by the user

settings.label: Validate instrumented shaders
settings.description: Run spirv-val after doing shader instrumentation

settings.label: Dump instrumented shaders
settings.description: Will dump the instrumented shaders (before and after) to working directory

settings.label: Limit how many time a pass can instrument the SPIR-V
settings.description: Zero is same as unlimited

settings.label: Print SPIR-V instrumentation info
settings.description: Prints verbose information about the instrumentation of the SPIR-V

settings.label: Disable DontInline performance boost
settings.description: Disable DontInline SPIR-V function hint for instrumentations functions, at the cost of a performance boost if the driver supports it. This flag can provoke instabilities on some drivers. Currently a debug option until we learn more about these instabilities.

settings.label: GPU Dump
settings.description: Similar to API Dump, but using all the state tracking information, print out information for GPU centric extensions.

messages.informative: Do you want to add 'warning' level to 'Message Severity'?

settings.label: Redirect all GPU Dump to stdout
settings.description: Instead of using the debug callback with information severity, redirect to stdout instead.

settings.label: Descriptor Hashing
settings.description: When enabled and using VK_EXT_descriptor_heap/VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer, this will attempt to track all descriptors seen such that GPU-AV and GPU Dump can detect more errors. This will increase the memory footprint.

settings.label: Total expected descriptors used
settings.description: We create a static allocation to hold all potential descriptor hashes we see. The larger it is the more memory and time it may take. The true capacity is always this value rounded up to the next power of two.

settings.label: Debug Printf only preset
settings.description: A single, quick setting to turn on only DebugPrintf and turn off everything else. Main usage is for people not able to use VkConfig and still want a fast preset to use.

settings.label: Debug Printf
settings.description: Enable DebugPrintf and will print anything use NonSemantic.DebugPrintf in their SPIR-V

settings.label: Redirect Printf messages to stdout
settings.description: Enable redirection of Debug Printf messages from the debug callback to stdout

messages.description: Enabling Debug Printf without stdout redirection, but 'info' level message severity is disabled, so printf message won't be shown.
messages.informative: Do you want to add 'info' level to 'Message Severity'?

settings.label: Printf verbose
settings.description: Will print out handles, instruction location, position in command buffer, and more

settings.label: Printf buffer size
settings.description: Set the size in bytes of the buffer per VkCommandBuffer to hold the messages (Each message is about 50 bytes)

messages.title: Warning: Debug Printf without info level message severity flag
messages.description: Enabling Debug Printf, but info level message severity is disabled, so printf message won't be shown.
messages.informative: Do you want to add 'info' level to 'Message Severity'?

settings.label: Debug Action
settings.description: Specifies what action is to be taken when a layer reports information

flags.label: Log Message

layer.name: VK_LAYER_LUNARG_monitor

layer.name: VK_LAYER_LUNARG_screenshot
layer.introduction: The screenshot layer records frames to image files.

settings.label: Frames
settings.description: Specifies list of frames to output as screenshots. It is specified as a comma-separated list of frames or a range of frames with a start, count, and optional interval separated by a dash. Setting the variable to "all" will output every frame. Example: "5-8-2" will output frame 5, continue until frame 13, dumping every other frame. Example: "3,8-2" will output frames 3, 8, and 9. If it is not set or it set to an empty string, no screenshots are created.

settings.label: Directory
settings.description: Specifies the directory in which to create the screenshot files. If it is not set or is set to an empty string, the files will be created in the current working directory.

settings.label: Format
settings.description: Specify a color space for the output. If it is not set, set to null, or set to USE_SWAPCHAIN_COLORSPACE the format will be set to use the same color space as the swapchain object.

settings.label: multisampleArrayImage
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports a VkImage being created as a 2D array with multiple samples per texel.

settings.label: mutableComparisonSamplers
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation allows descriptors with comparison samplers to be updated.

settings.label: pointPolygons
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports Rasterization using a point Polygon Mode.

settings.label: samplerMipLodBias
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports setting a mipmap LOD bias value when creating a sampler.

settings.label: separateStencilMaskRef
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports separate front and back Stencil Test reference values.

settings.label: shaderSampleRateInterpolationFunctions
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports fragment shaders which use the InterpolationFunction capability.

settings.label: tessellationIsolines
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports isoline output from the Tessellation stage of a graphics pipeline. This member is only meaningful if tessellationShader are supported.

settings.label: triangleFans
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports Triangle Fans primitive topology.

settings.label: vertexAttributeAccessBeyondStride
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports accessing a vertex input attribute beyond the stride of the corresponding vertex input binding.

settings.label: minVertexInputBindingStrideAlignment
settings.description: Indicates whether this implementation supports accessing a vertex input attribute beyond the stride of the corresponding vertex input binding.

settings.label: Exclude Device Extensions
settings.description: Removes the listed device extensions from being reported by the Vulkan physical device.

settings.label: Exclude Formats
settings.description: Removes the format feature flags from being reported by the Vulkan physical device.

settings.label: Debug Actions
settings.description: This indicates what action is to be taken when a layer wants to report information

flags.label: Log to stdout
flags.description: Log messages using the stdout.

flags.label: Log to OutputDebugString
flags.description: Log messages using the Windows OutputDebugString for Vulkan Studio output display.

flags.label: Log to File
flags.description: Log messages to a file.

settings.label: Log Filename
settings.description: Specifies the output filename

settings.label: Clear Log at Launch
settings.description: Discard the content of the log file between each layer run

flags.label: Break
flags.description: Trigger a breakpoint if a debugger is in use.

settings.label: Fail on Error
settings.description: If the device doesn't support the capabilities of the selected Profile, the layer fail to load. When enabled, vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices will fail when the selected Profile is not supported.

settings.label: Message Types
settings.description: This is a comma-delineated list of options telling the layer what types of messages it should report back

flags.label: Notification
flags.description: Report notifications.

flags.label: Warning
flags.description: Report warnings from using the API in a manner which may lead to undefined behavior or to warn the user of common trouble spots. A warning does NOT necessarily signify illegal application behavior.

flags.label: Error
flags.description: Report errors in API usage.

flags.label: Debug
flags.description: Report debug information for the Profiles Layer development.

settings.label: Force Enable
settings.description: Force the layer to be active even if the underlying driver also implements the shader object extension.

settings.label: Disable Pipeline Pre-Caching
settings.description: Disable the layer from pre-caching pipelines, reducing the memory overhead.

layer.name: VK_LAYER_LUNARG_crash_diagnostic
layer.description: Crash Diagnostic Layer is a crash/hang debugging tool that helps determines GPU progress in a Vulkan application.

settings.label: State Tracking
settings.description: Control of state tracking.

settings.label: Synchronize commands
settings.description: Add pipeline barriers after instrumented commands to help identify whether a Vulkan crash is due to a synchronization issue.
settings.detailed: VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering usage is required for this feature otherwise Validation layer errors will be generated.

messages.title: 'Synchronize commands' is incompatible with Vulkan RenderPass
messages.description: 'Synchronize commands' add pipeline barriers after instrumented commands. This feature is not supported for Vulkan application using Vulkan RenderPass which would generate Validation layer errors.
messages.informative: Are you sure you want to enable 'Synchronize commands'?

settings.label: Add markers on each Vulkan command
settings.description: Include completion markers around every vulkan command
settings.detailed: This may allow more accuratute fault locations at the expense of larger command buffers and reduced performance

settings.label: Crash dump file
settings.description: Control of dump files

settings.label: Output Path
settings.description: The directory where dump files and shader binaries are written.

settings.label: Crash Dump Triggers
settings.description: Additional crash detection methods beyond a VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST error returned by the Vulkan driver.

settings.label: Watchdog Timer
settings.description: If the application fails to submit new commands within a set time, a crash dump will be created as if the a lost device error was encountered.

settings.label: Watchdog Timeout (ms)
settings.description: Time in milliseconds the application has to submit a new command before creating a crash dump.

settings.label: Dump semaphores
settings.description: Include semaphore state reporting in runtime logging and crash dump files

settings.label: Dump queue submissions
settings.description: Control which queue submissions are included in the dump.

flags.label: Running
flags.description: Submissions that were executing at the time of the dump.

flags.label: Pending
flags.description: Submissions executing or pending at the time of the dump.

settings.label: Dump command buffers
settings.description: Control which command buffers are included in the dump.

flags.label: Running
flags.description: Command Buffers that were executing at the time of the dump.

flags.label: Pending
flags.description: Command Buffers executing or pending at the time of the dump.

flags.label: All
flags.description: All known Command Buffers.

settings.label: Dump commands
settings.description: Control which commands are included in the dump.

flags.label: Running
flags.description: Command Buffers that were executing at the time of the dump.

flags.label: Pending
flags.description: Commands executing or pending at the time of the dump.

flags.label: All
flags.description: All known Commands.

settings.label: Dump shaders
settings.description: Control of shader dumping.

flags.label: Off
flags.description: Never dump shaders.

flags.label: On Crash
flags.description: Dump currently bound shaders after a crash is detected.

flags.label: On Bind
flags.description: Dump only bound shaders.

flags.label: All
flags.description: Dump all shaders.

settings.label: Logging
settings.description: Control of logging

settings.label: Log Filename
settings.description: none = no logging, stderr or stdout = to the console, otherwise an absolute or relative path.

settings.label: Log main submission and synchronization Vulkan commands
settings.description: Add Vulkan API calls intercepted by the layer will be logged to the console.
settings.detailed: This includes: vkDeviceWaitIdle, vkQueueWaitIdle, vkQueuePresentKHR, vkWaitForFences, vkGetFenceStatus, vkAcquireNextImageKHR, vkCreateCommandPool, vkDestroyCommandPool, vkResetCommandPool, vkAllocateCommandBuffers, vkFreeCommandBuffers, vkQueueSubmit, vkQueueSubmit2, vkQueueSubmit2KHR and vkQueueBindSparse

settings.label: Log Vulkan commands that use semaphores
settings.description: Add logging messages about every vulkan command that uses semaphores

messages.title: 'Log Vulkan commands that use semaphores' requires 'Track semaphores' to be enabled
messages.description: 'Log Vulkan commands that use semaphores' requires 'Track semaphores' to be enabled
messages.informative: Are you sure you want to enable 'Log Vulkan commands that use semaphores'?

settings.label: Message Severity
settings.description: Comma-delineated list of options specifying the types of log messages to be reported.

flags.label: Error
flags.description: Report errors such as device lost or setup problems in the layer.

flags.label: Warning
flags.description: Report non-fatal problems that may interfere with operation of the layer

flags.label: Info
flags.description: Report informational messages.

flags.label: Debug
flags.description: For layer development. Report messages for debugging layer behavior.
